validated_learning.title: Corporate crypto treasury headlines are not executable-flow equivalents
observed_facts: Strategy acquired $2.01B of BTC during May 11-17 while BTC fell about 5.7% from the prior close through period-end; the disclosed purchase was roughly 6.2% of one average day's reported BTC turnover.

Strategy's BTC Monetization Program was publicly filed at 08:00:15 ET on June 29. Strategy then sold $216M of BTC through July 5 for preferred-distribution/USD-reserve purposes while BTC rose about 5.7% over the sale window.

KULR sold 333 BTC in open-market transactions during July 9-23 to repay a $20M Coinbase credit facility while BTC rose about 2.9%; it later sold the remaining approximately 764 BTC during Aug. 20-Sep. 11 while BTC also rose over that interval.

SharpLink disclosed a $75M financing after the June 23 close with stated intent to acquire ETH; it bought 10,000 ETH for $16.1M during June 24-26 while ETH fell about 5.3%. The actual immediate ETH purchase used only a minority of net offering proceeds.
Upexi increased its treasury by 265,500 locked SOL through an in-kind contribution for a convertible note, explicitly without an immediate on-chain transfer, validator exit or unstaking.

BitMine disclosed weekly ETH acquisitions of 32,447 ETH and 53,501 ETH in consecutive weeks; the smaller-buy week coincided with a large ETH rise while the larger-buy week coincided with a slight decline.

An exploratory 10-event Strategy BTC-buy panel had 6 positive and 4 negative interval returns. Purchase scale versus one average day's reported turnover had weak Pearson (~0.23) and Spearman (~0.21) association with interval return. A broader selected 16-event buy/sell panel aligned with the naive buy-up/sell-down sign only 7 times. These are negative controls, not calibrated estimates.
validated_learning.inference: Financing capacity, realized financing, treasury holdings change and executable signed underlying flow must be represented as separate causal states. Even real acquisition/disposition can be dominated by competing flows and macro/derivatives/ETF conditions. Reported turnover is a rough scale denominator rather than market depth.
validated_learning.method_rule: Normalize treasury events as financing authorization/capacity -> realized net financing -> declared allocation -> actual buy/sell -> execution mode -> public disclosure timestamp -> flow versus usable depth/free float -> competing flows -> price response. Do not treat a treasury headline or holdings delta as a standalone directional predictor.
limitations: Exact within-window order timestamps are often unavailable.
OTC, in-kind, locked, staked or hedged execution can differ from visible exchange flow.
Close-to-close windows can miss intraday impact.
The event panel is small/selected and unsuitable for causal effect-size estimation.

pre_move_predictor_tests.evidence: Public 8-K said net proceeds were intended for ETH/general working capital; actual 10,000 ETH purchase occurred June 24-26.
pre_move_predictor_tests.outcome: ETH fell over the execution interval.
pre_move_predictor_tests.lesson: Public use-of-proceeds intent still requires realized allocation size, execution mode and competing-flow context before forecasting price direction.

pre_move_predictor_tests.evidence: Program created sale authority; Strategy subsequently disclosed $216M of actual BTC sales through July 5.
pre_move_predictor_tests.outcome: BTC rose over the sale window.
pre_move_predictor_tests.lesson: Public sell authority plus realized selling does not mechanically imply negative interval return.

pre_move_predictor_tests.evidence: KULR stated it may sell BTC instead of issuing equity to fund operations; actual open-market sales began July 9.
pre_move_predictor_tests.outcome: BTC rose during the July 9-23 sale interval.
pre_move_predictor_tests.lesson: Authorization is a conditional supply option; operating cash needs/debt constraints determine realization.
